# HISTORY — `experiments/mjc`

*Auto-generated big-history summary. Overwrite freely; do not hand-edit expecting persistence.*

## Origin and founding discipline (2026-07-16)

`mjc` was proposed in [`ideas/physical_control_substrate.md`](../../ideas/physical_control_substrate.md) as a third controllable-dynamics DGP, one rung of realism above RHM/MNIST-reaching and below language — motivated by asking where a "vanilla" scaling+imitation robot policy is *structurally* confounded (prompted by reading Sunday Robotics' ACT-2 preview). The memo drew one fork early and the whole node has held it since: **controllable-dynamics DGP, not RL-to-SOTA benchmark**. Policies are obtained cheaply (scripted/MPC/short imitation); every experiment is a knob sweep against a vanilla baseline, so the deliverable is always a *slope or dissociation*, never a leaderboard number. This is the same discipline RHM runs, transplanted onto continuous contact dynamics.

The founding memo pitched five cuts, cheapest first, and cut #5 — "drifting dynamics as a *novelty generator*" for dimensionality expansion — was billed as *"the single biggest open question of the whole program."* That framing would stand unrun for over a year of narrative time and eventually be run and retired (see below) — one of the cleanest arcs of the whole node.

## Cuts #1–#3: establishing the substrate is trustworthy (2026-07-16)

Three foundational cuts landed same-day, each retiring a confound rather than chasing a headline number: [`contact_residual/`](contact_residual/README.md) (Cut #1) found the FM residual concentrates at contact events specifically (an *event* detector, not a state detector) — but only after learning that **Huber, not MSE** was required, or contact's heavy tail starves free-flight learning. [`arity_torque/`](arity_torque/README.md) (Cut #2) showed arity beats resolution once the received-wisdom confound (correlated commands) was killed via i.i.d. control — the smallest command-aware model beat the largest command-blind one. [`dynamics_shift/`](dynamics_shift/README.md) (Cut #3) reframed a shaky "degradation slope" idea into the arc's load-bearing finding: intervening on the transition operator (not the task) lets a model-based agent re-adapt from ~50 reward-free transitions while a matched model-free policy needs ~240× more reward-labeled data — gated by re-groundability. **This cut's substrate — reward-free re-adaptation of a world-model factor — is what nearly everything downstream is built on top of.**

A naming decision from this period is still load-bearing: the package is `mjc`, not `mujoco`, because a local `mujoco` package would shadow the real pip package on Modal's `sys.path`.

## The value↔FM interface arc: from a stationary control to a phenomenon-first pivot

The next arc asked how a value signal should shape a forward model, motivated by [`ideas/two_timescale_value_loop.md`](../../ideas/two_timescale_value_loop.md)'s claim that the a2a program built forward models and one-shot value heads but never a *non-stationary, reward-driven outer loop*. [`value_shaping/`](value_shaping/README.md) established the stationary control: value re-allocates a capacity-limited FM away from a reducible-but-irrelevant force field, robust in its core claim but with fragile "teeth" (a data-scarcity effect). [`directed_readapt/`](directed_readapt/README.md) then delivered **two instructive negatives** rather than a positive: a global shift has no scarcity to exploit, and a localized shift has scarcity but the disagreement-based drive is blind to a confident-but-wrong prior. This negative result is a hinge in the node's thinking — it is cited explicitly as what **"motivates the pivot to phenomenon-first work"** rather than chasing a single directed-collection mechanism.

That pivot became [`meta_adapt/`](meta_adapt/README.md), the arc's most sustained single node (#4 → #4e, five sub-cuts). It methodically separated claims that had been conflated: a 1-D damping floor collapses under meta-learning (the RHM anchor: meta-learning buys nothing when there's no compositional structure to exploit) while an actuator-rotation conflict opens the meta/multitask gap monotonically (#4); an explicit context latent can decode the task parameter with system-ID R²≈1.0 *independent of* whether that identification helps adaptation (#4b); value-directed identification is a robust scarcity-gated negative (#4c); value-shaping and meta-conditioning are separable capacity levers that combine only under capacity competition (#4d); and closing the reward loop end-to-end reproduces the hand-designed value allocation from reward alone, with a wireheading gotcha (normalize the weight budget, or the loop games loss-scale) (#4e).

[`curiosity_control/`](curiosity_control/README.md) supplied the complementary *afferent* half (where to collect) to #4d/#4e's *efferent* half (what to model): a curiosity drive tracks a moving reducible frontier but exhibits a **noisy-TV pathology** on low-dim control — a substrate inversion of the a2a active-vision result — cured only by grounding curiosity with an exploit signal as two additive drives.

## The keystone attempt and its obstruction — a productive negative result

[`online_value_loop/`](online_value_loop/README.md) tried to build the arc's actual keystone: a fully-online two-timescale loop where reward continuously shapes a *live* FM, tested on both the afferent and efferent levers. Both were obstructed — CEM-MPC control turned out robust to the curiosity drive's tracking benefit, and the value-shaping benefit was only a slow, commit-dependent, pre-convergence transient. The node's own read of this: **the obstruction is a positive confirmation, not a dead end** — it means value is fundamentally a slow/committed quantity, so the two-timescale split is *forced* rather than a design choice, and named the next experiment. [`drift_value_loop/`](drift_value_loop/README.md) took that hint under perpetual drift and, across three cuts, isolated that compounding across drift comes from *memory* (a context-latent), not from value-carving itself, and that the missing ingredient all along was **the teacher** — grading the meta-loop by value-relevant FM prediction-error rather than by control performance produces a clean interior explore/exploit optimum. **"The teacher, not the structure"** is one of the node's most-repeated conclusions from this period.

## Ballistic control: the mechanism that explains why value kept failing to transmit

[`ballistic/`](ballistic/README.md) supplied the missing mechanistic piece: replanning is a **blind grader** of FM quality, because re-grounding every step papers over a stale model. Recasting control as feedforward/committed rather than reactive — the biologically forced regime, since you can't replan faster than sensorimotor delay — made the FM ~3× more behaviorally load-bearing and made reward-free re-adaptation ~4.3× more valuable after a drift. This reframes several earlier obstructions (in `directed_readapt/`, `online_value_loop/`) as consequences of testing under the wrong control mode, not as failures of the value idea. Its child [`ballistic/directed/`](ballistic/directed/README.md) built a directed-collection ladder (learning-progress × visitation) that worked — but its sharpest cut (S2) was later **retracted** for a 22× measurement subsidy: the monitor that decided where to look was itself unmetered, silently smuggling in free global surveillance. That retraction became its own thread (see E3, below).

## The collection-realism turn: teleportation was the substrate's standing unrealism

Running alongside the value arc, [`on_policy/`](on_policy/README.md) confronted a foundational assumption: nearly every prior cut trained on *teleported* (`set_state`-based) transitions — free, omniscient, discontinuous. The standing memo [`on_policy/COLLECTION_REALISM.md`](on_policy/COLLECTION_REALISM.md) sorted every prior claim into three tiers (safe dissociations, inflated absolute sample-counts, and previously-unaskable allocation questions), then built `collection_mode="on_policy"` as an additive flag with a metered `Body` abstraction (no `set_state` exposed) and a bit-identical teleport path. Three experiments (E0–E2) priced the cost: most of on-policy's *apparent* advantage was a mistuned teleport knob (E0); a **global** drift is re-adaptable equally well on-policy or not (E1, refuting the arc's own hypothesis that embodiment would matter here); but a **local** drift makes embodiment genuinely load-bearing — on-policy needs 2.5× more transitions and broad teleport never repairs the region at all (E2). **Net: embodiment is free when structure is global, expensive when local** — and this is now the default collection convention for new cuts, while teleport stays the permanent code default for reproducibility. This convention shift (2026-07-23) is one of the node's clearest examples of updating a standing practice without breaking backward compatibility.

[`on_policy/directed_on_policy/`](on_policy/directed_on_policy/README.md) (E3) then re-attempted `ballistic/directed`'s retracted S2 question with the monitor itself metered (ratio 1.84× vs S2's 22×) — the first setup where "where should I practice?" is genuinely askable on-policy. Both halves of the ladder reproduced across seeds: relevance pays once looking is embodied, and reducibility-awareness pays (an error-only drive burns 47% of its budget on the noisy-TV trap this substrate reintroduces).

## Cut #5, finally run: dimensionality expansion, and a hypothesis retired

[`expansion/`](expansion/README.md) closed the node's oldest open question, over a year after it was proposed. Built as *calibrate → measure → calibrate* because rank-shaped instruments had already failed three times in this repo (a lesson imported from [`beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md`](../../beliefs/dimensionality_expansion.md), whose own arithmetic decomposition was independently falsified and replaced with a shape/level pair — β and `R_res_participation` — around the same date). The result: drifting a plant's physics does **not** open a forward model's representable directions (±0.08, against a genuine +0.72±0.42 calibration on the same plant and instrument — a real effect ~10× larger, ruling out instrument-insensitivity as the explanation). This **retires the founding memo's own motivating claim** that "drifting dynamics is a novelty generator." The belief tree was updated in the same sitting to scope dimensionality expansion to domains with hierarchical structure to expand *into* — a fixed-DOF motor plant is not one, and animal biology (bodies don't grow limbs) is read as corroborating evidence rather than decoration. What survives explicitly: drift remains essential to the whole `drift_value_loop`/`on_policy` line for **realism**, just not for representational growth; and instrument-level findings (β unusable at low state-dimension; the readout is degenerate at both saturation and divergence) outlive the closed cut.

[`arm_substrate/`](arm_substrate/README.md) was built alongside this period as pure machinery — a second task family retiring the ballistic arc's single-family caveat, verifying every precondition (capacity binds only at n≥5; ballistic transmits 6.0× vs reactive; a passive tool locates the capacity-competition boundary in kg) before any cut was ported onto it.

## The conceptual synthesis that ties the arc together (2026-07-25)

[`ideas/heterogeneous_graders.md`](../../ideas/heterogeneous_graders.md) is the node's clearest instance of "reading between the lines": rather than a new experiment, it re-reads nearly everything above as five conditions that distinguish motor learning from distribution modeling (commitment under delay, metered measurement, endogenous data, Type-2 non-stationarity, two different-type teachers) — each already priced by a specific `mjc` result — and argues the deeper claim is that **no single learning signal can be both dense and evaluative**, so a two-teacher structure is forced, not designed. This same dichotomy is read from the representation side in the dimensionality-expansion belief's own update: compression is dense-gradeable, expansion is not. The synthesis explicitly names E3 and the ballistic/directed retraction as unfinished business it expects the node to resolve next.

## Where the thread stands

As of the most recent commits (2026-07-27), the live thread is finishing E3's on-policy re-attempt of the retracted S2 directed-collection question, and asking whether ensemble disagreement — which S1 found useless when every model has data everywhere — recovers its diagnostic job once on-policy collection creates genuinely unvisited territory. The belief-tree back-translation (value is slow/committed; the teacher, not the structure; control mode gates transmission) is flagged as owed but not yet written. The overall shape of this node's ~2-week narrative: found a trustworthy substrate → tried to build a value-driven learning loop and kept discovering *why* it wasn't transmitting (control mode, the grader, the teacher) → discovered its own data-collection assumption was unrealistic and fixed that as a parallel axis → and finally closed its oldest, most ambitious open question with a clean null that forced a real retraction of the founding motivation, not just a footnote.
